subject: Finite stable-phase abstraction generated from the compiled Boatstack ControlProgram registry. It contains one event for every runtime entry and expands each declared source and target phase set. The 18-facet predicates, operating-system behavior, and external-provider truth remain executable evidence obligations rather than theorem assumptions.

evidence.note: Compiler combines exact CoreSystem, PrimaryFlow, extension, contract, and ownership declarations into one immutable runtime registry.
Generated readable projection from the same runtime registry.
Exact admission, authority, parameter, source-revision, provider-request, expiry, and stale-snapshot checks.
Single apply path across lock, journal, effect, fresh observation, target predicate, receipt, and recovery.
Admitted native effects reduce every controllable Standard distribution transition through one state adapter.
Runtime facet/event classification, writer-boundary inventory, and reducer-completeness refusing tests.
Exact-admission, stale-snapshot, postcondition, interruption, idempotency, and unknown-outcome tests.
Staged effect ordering, atomic resource application, rollback, and external settlement boundary.
Historical incidents resolved through the executable runtime supervisor.

spec.description: Every reachable stable catalog phase retains a path to terminal, explicit frontier, or safe abandonment.

unknowns: The stable-phase graph is a conservative expansion of declared source and target phase sets; facet combinations and deterministic reducer branches remain executable-test obligations.
External provider state and operating-system crash behavior are represented by declared outcomes and restart tests, not exhaustively observed by Locus.
